audit.why: Slow melee tank who farms with Vorpal Spikes (E) and answers your walk-up with Rupture (Q). Lane is Aatrox's, but he cannot force through Feral Scream (W) on cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase text was a generic template that named no ultimate and no cooldown.
audit.why: Feast (R) is 80/70/60 and deals true damage that ignores every resistance you buy. World Ender (120/100/80) is the longer cooldown, so never trade R for R at low health.
audit.corrected: Feast (R) is true damage on an 80s cooldown and ignores every resistance you buy — never sit low against it. World Ender's heal amp is how you climb out of a Rupture chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions described Infernal Chains (W) as a root; Riot’s text says enemies are dragged back to the centre if they do not leave the zone, and the decisive interaction for this matchup was absent.
audit.why: Rupture (Q, 6s flat) knocks you into the air and slows — airborne cancels Umbral Dash, so it is the tool that denies your mobility. Feral Scream (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9) silences, which locks your whole kit including E.
audit.corrected: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto Cho'Gath. Infernal Chains (W) drags him back to the centre if he doesn't leave the zone. Rupture (Q, 6s flat) pops you airborne and denies your dash, and Feral Scream (W, 11s at rank 1) silences your whole kit — step up on those two cooldowns. Feast is true damage: never sit low.

edits.before: Ultimate interaction changes all-ins. At level 6, reassess the matchup. Aatrox gains his ultimate, but Cho'Gath's ultimate or scaling pattern may change whether you can commit.
edits.after: Feast (R) is true damage on an 80s cooldown and ignores every resistance you buy — never sit low against it. World Ender's heal amp is how you climb out of a Rupture chain.
